contract.anchor: ## 18. PHASE-MANTA-B2B route-semantics and responsive correction — R2

active_phase.immediate_objective: PHASE-MANTA-B2B-ROUTE-SEMANTICS-AND-RESPONSIVE-VISUAL-CORRECTION-R2 corrected the four architect-identified acceptance blockers of the already-published PHASE-MANTA-B2B implementation, with ZERO migrations and db/** byte-unchanged, and the phase now awaits architect technical AND visual ACCEPTANCE. It is NOT accepted and NOT self-accepted. D1 CLOSED: a mixed Pedido no longer renders the union of its two routes as one client stepper - js/product-route.js gained splitClientStepsByRoute (one INDEPENDENT step list per applicable route, ordered Tapete then Manta, each entry carrying the route-local displayIndex), js/pedido-tracking-ui.js gained getClienteTrackingSectionsForRoutes and getClienteTrackingRoutePosition, and the new cohesive module js/screens/cliente-route-sections-ui.js arranges one visibly identified section per route ('Rota Tapete' / 'Rota Manta') with its own stepper, connectors and partial percentages; the pre-existing filterClientSteps union function is retained UNCHANGED for aggregate consumers but is no longer the input of a rendering surface. ROOT CAUSE of D1: R1 made the SHAPE of the client steps route-derived but kept a single stepper fed by the union, which for a mixed Pedido necessarily contains acabamento, so the Manta half of the order was shown a finishing step its route does not have. D2 CLOSED: buildStepNode printed String(index+1) where index is the CANONICAL position in the full eight-step list, so a Manta route rendered 1,2,3,4,6,7,8 - a visible gap exactly where acabamento was filtered out; the visible ordinal is now the route-local position (pos+1) while the canonical index remains the authority for progress comparison, DTO lookup and state resolution and is no longer printed, and connectors are coloured from route-local adjacency instead of canonical adjacency. No hidden Acabamento node was fabricated. Proved live: Manta 1..7 with canonical [0,1,2,3,5,6,7], Tapete 1..8 with canonical [0..7]; the administrative route sections number 1..4 for Manta and 1..5 for Tapete. D3 CLOSED FOR THE REQUIRED B2B SURFACES ONLY: D3 is a route-neutral PLATFORM defect - the global chrome in js/screens/common.js is built with INLINE style attributes (196px sidebar, 62px topbar, flex row) and the repository had NO media-query infrastructure at all, so an inline declaration outranked any stylesheet rule and no breakpoint could exist; at 375px the sidebar consumed 196px of the viewport and left the cockpit grid a 131px content column with paragraphs collapsing to ~1.2 words per line, and expedicao-admin.js buildItens appended 720px-wide rows DIRECTLY into a card with overflow:hidden so those columns were clipped with no reachable scroll. The correction adds css/responsive.css - the repository's first media queries - anchored EXCLUSIVELY on data-rv-* REGION attributes with deliberate !important (a plain rule would be inert against the inline chrome, and the responsive smoke test pins that reasoning): below 768px the shell stacks and the SAME navigation items become a horizontally scrollable strip through the SAME navItem mechanism (no drawer, no hamburger, no overlay - the global navigation was NOT redesigned); below 1024px the cockpit collapses to one column, the right rail loses sticky and lays out BELOW the main column, the two-column card grids collapse and the route stepper stacks so no route node is clipped or overlapped; wide tables scroll inside containers they OWN at every width, including the expedition item table which now receives its rows in a data-rv-table-scroll container instead of the overflow:hidden card; metric grids drop to two columns, fixed-px form grids stack, and the client stepper scrolls in its own container with a legible min-width instead of compressing labels. Measured in a REAL browser across nine surfaces at 1440/785/375px: documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth on EVERY one, so document-level horizontal overflow is 0px throughout and the documented 19px overflow at the 785px route boundary is gone; every element still wider than the viewport sits inside an owned scroll container, which the order permits; the narrowest multi-word text block improved from 1.2 to at least 2.3 words per line. The application is NOT claimed to be globally responsive - only the enumerated B2B surfaces were corrected and measured, and js/screens/op-nova.js (same cockpit grid for the 'aberta' weaving-OP state) lies OUTSIDE this order's authorized paths and was deliberately left untouched. D4 CLOSED: four distinct false statements, all from conflating the production STAGE (ops.tipo) with the product ROUTE (modelos.tipo_produto) at the PRESENTATION layer, which R1 corrected structurally but not in vocabulary. The weaving-OP summary builder now takes the route EXPLICITLY (buildResumo(totais, route) selecting from a RESUMO_LABELS table, never guessing) and reads 'Saida medida' for Manta while Tapete keeps 'Entregue p/ acabamento' and its original percentage sentence verbatim; buildPedidoSummaryMetrics SUPPRESSES the aggregate 'Em acabamento' metric for a Manta-only Pedido rather than rendering it as zero (zero would assert that the stage exists) and replaces it with the true metric 'Saida medida (Manta)', while for a mixed Pedido both appear side by side and emAcabamento continues to sum only stageKey==='acabamento' summaries - that is ops.tipo='latex', where no Manta can exist by DB guarantee - so it contains TAPETE VALUES ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION (proved on the mixed fixture: emAcabamento 300 with mantaMedido 180 held separately); the item table emits the ACABAMENTO column only when an applicable route has the stage and renders an em-dash with an explanatory title for a Manta row in a mixed Pedido, and the Manta released/delivered VALUES were corrected because on the Manta route the expedition references the op_item of the WEAVING OP, so a Manta item with 90m released and 30m delivered now reads prontos 60 / entregues 30 instead of 0/0; OP_CARD_LABELS gives a Manta weaving card 'Saida medida' and a 'Movimentar para Expedicao' modal while Tapete keeps every string verbatim; and the documentary logic, extracted to buildOpDocBanner and buildOpDocumentRow in pedido-route-sections.js, emits NO pendency for a Manta weaving OP - the tone is neutral and the text states that the route has no movement to finishing, an explanatory note rather than a manufactured requirement - with the document row citing the transition the route actually has, Tecelagem -> Expedicao. NO NEW DOCUMENT TYPE was invented: where the existing document contract defines no requirement for the Manta measured output the false pendency is OMITTED, and every Tapete banner and row string is byte-identical to before. ACCEPTED LIMITATION, explicitly recorded: status_cliente_visual is a Pedido-level curated commercial artefact owned by db/30 and this order authorizes NO migration, so a per-route PUBLISHED position does not exist; what is computed per route is the step set, the visible numbering, the per-step state, the connector colours, the partial-DTO match (by key, and only within the route that owns the key) and a route-local reached/next note. Client permission boundaries are preserved verbatim: cliente-pedido-detail.js still performs NO direct read, the routes still arrive from the dedicated reader cliente-route-read.js, no administrative datum is exposed and no permission is broadened. STRUCTURE: pedido-detail-events.js stayed at exactly 2709 lines and pedido-detail-progress.js fell from 919 to 918, so neither protected file grew - the route-aware documentary and summary derivations were EXTRACTED into js/screens/pedido-route-sections.js (448 to 538) rather than appended; pedido-detail-render.js 1333 to 1424 and op-tecelagem-producao-admin.js 782 to 800 remain single cohesive screens below the exceptional limit; the two new files (css/responsive.css and js/screens/cliente-route-sections-ui.js at 105 lines) are well under 500 lines; no DML in any render module, no new direct table write, every Manta write still an authoritative RPC through manta-writes.js, index.html still declarative with every changed asset cache-bumped, and CODE-HEALTH-AUDIT-18-R1 was not enlarged. EVIDENCE: tests/manta-route-ui.smoke.js extended with fifteen R2 proofs to 48 green assertions and new tests/responsive-layout.smoke.js with 21 green assertions together cover all EIGHTEEN numbered requirements of the order's test contract, including runtime rendering of the client card for Manta-only, Tapete-only and mixed route sets; full suite node --test tests/**/*.js reports 4239 tests and the set of failing test NAMES is a STRICT SUBSET of the bbd5f85 baseline set, proved by name-level diff against a clean detached worktree at bbd5f85 - ZERO INTRODUCED FAILURES - with per-file confirmation in the canonical workspace that pedido-detail 41->41, tec-to-acabamento-flow 2->2, production-flow-invariants 1->1, screens-common 8->8, cliente-portal-visual 9->9 and entrega-writes 1->1 fail under identical names; no existing Tapete assertion was weakened or removed, and the two static assertions whose subject moved were realigned with one of them made STRICTER (positional DTO matching is now forbidden outright) while the other stopped freezing a literal cache-bust value that the order itself mandates bumping. Visual validation ran against a DISPOSABLE untracked in-browser fixture loading the real product modules with a purely in-memory read double - no network, no Supabase project, no Vercel, no fabricated session, no real business data - and the fixture and its local static server were destroyed with zero repository residue; pixel captures were taken and directly inspected at 1440/785/375px and are not committed. Architect technical and visual acceptance remains PENDING. Shared development ucrjtfswnfdlxwtmxnoo was NOT accessed and remains at terminal 84 with the Manta backend dormant; PHASE-MANTA-B2A (db/85-88) still awaits its own architect review; PHASE-MANTA-B2C remains unauthorized. Business-flow recreation remains paused.
